sections.title: Nonuniqueness of Solutions to 2D Incompressible Euler Equations with Unbounded Vorticity
sections.abstract: The author constructs two distinct finite-energy weak solutions of planar incompressible Euler from the same compactly supported, mean-zero vorticity lying in every finite Lp, using a cascade of quadrupole transitions across infinitely many scales.
sections.claimed_result: The author proves existence of two distinct global renormalized vorticity-transport solutions, also weak momentum solutions, with the same initial vorticity in every finite Lp and velocities continuous in L2; the solutions differ at time 1.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Two-dimensional unforced Euler on R2; initial vorticity is compactly supported, mean zero, and belongs to the intersection of all finite Lp spaces; bounded vorticity is not asserted.
sections.unique_caveat: The paper notes that its constructed Lp-norm growth does not establish sharpness of the Yudovich uniqueness condition.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Concrete nonuniqueness result in a central PDE problem; introduction and theorem statement checked. Placement reflects potential mathematical significance rather than measured readership.

sections.title: Sharp approximations for the stationary measures of the open ASEP I: The shock region
sections.abstract: The authors interpret the Bryc polynomial in open ASEP through a birth–death Markov chain and obtain sharp total-variation approximations by Bernoulli product measures in the high- and low-density phases of the shock region, with moderate-deviation applications.
sections.claimed_result: The authors establish the stated total-variation approximations and derive moderate-deviation estimates for the stationary measure and asymptotic results for open ASEP with light particles.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Open asymmetric simple exclusion process with boundary interactions, in the high- and low-density phases of the shock region.
sections.unique_caveat: The sharp Bernoulli approximations are restricted to the shock region’s high- and low-density phases.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: First installment of a three-paper result series; combines a probabilistic representation with sharp stationary-law estimates and is cross-listed in probability and mathematical physics.

sections.title: Sharp approximations for the stationary measures of the open ASEP II: The coexistence line
sections.abstract: For open ASEP on the coexistence line, the authors identify an observable shock location, show its law is close in total variation to the uniform lattice law, and approximate occupation variables away from the shock by Bernoulli product measures conditional on that location.
sections.claimed_result: The authors prove the shock-location approximation and conditional product-measure approximation, yielding fluctuation limits, moderate-deviation bounds for particle density, and correlation-function limits.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Stationary open ASEP on its coexistence line; occupation variables are approximated away from the identified shock, conditional on its location.
sections.unique_caveat: The result is tied to the coexistence line and does not by itself cover the shock or fan regimes treated in companion papers.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Extends the cross-listed ASEP series with a precise shock-location law, optimal total-variation bounds, and stated fluctuation and correlation applications.

sections.title: Sharp approximations for the stationary measures of the open ASEP III: The fan region
sections.abstract: In the fan region of open ASEP, the authors obtain discrete Brownian-excursion/meander counterparts and Bernoulli product approximations, and prove moderate-deviation bounds for particle counts using path estimates and negative correlations.
sections.claimed_result: The authors prove total-variation approximations by lazy-random-walk excursions and meanders away from boundaries, exponentially accurate Bernoulli approximations in high- and low-density phases, and moderate deviations in the maximal-current phase and its fan-region boundaries.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Open ASEP with general boundary rates, in specified fan-region phases; excursion/meander approximation is stated away from boundaries.
sections.unique_caveat: The estimates are phase- and location-specific and do not assert one approximation uniformly across every regime.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Completes the three-part, probability/mathematical-physics series and treats a distinct stationary phase with explicit approximation and concentration results.

sections.title: Stationary measures of the open KPZ equation: A short proof
sections.abstract: The authors give a probabilistic proof of the two-layer Brownian representation for the stationary measure of open KPZ on a finite interval with arbitrary Neumann boundary parameters, using open-ASEP representations and weakly asymmetric limits.
sections.claimed_result: The authors give a short probabilistic derivation of the stationary two-layer Brownian representation using martingale estimates for Bryc polynomials and known convergence from open ASEP to open KPZ.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Open KPZ on a finite interval with arbitrary Neumann boundary parameters; derivation uses weakly asymmetric scaling and existing ASEP-to-KPZ convergence results.
sections.unique_caveat: This is a new proof of a representation already established by other authors, not a claim to be the first proof or a new general existence theorem.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Direct bridge from the same day’s ASEP series to KPZ; the abstract says the proof recovers a representation recently established in full generality.

sections.title: Sharp Stability of Brenier Potentials and its Link to Poincaré Inequalities
sections.abstract: The authors prove a functional inequality bounding the variance of differences of convex functions by Wasserstein distance between their gradient pushforwards, yielding sharp stability of Brenier potentials for uniformly log-concave sources.
sections.claimed_result: The authors prove the variance is at most kappa inverse times squared 2-Wasserstein distance between gradient pushforwards for a kappa-uniformly log-concave probability measure and convex potentials with gradients in L2.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: A fixed uniformly log-concave source probability measure on R-d; both potentials are convex and their gradients are square-integrable under the source.
sections.unique_caveat: Uniform log-concavity is substantive: the paper also gives log-concave measures for which the stronger Brenier stability inequality fails despite finite Poincaré constants.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Four-subfield cross-listing and checked main theorem connect functional inequalities, optimal transport, metric geometry, and probability; a sharp constant is proved under uniform log-concavity.

sections.title: Hodge--Riemann relations for nef bundles
sections.abstract: The authors introduce an (m,p,q)-Lefschetz framework and prove Hodge–Riemann relations for products of top Chern and derived Schur classes of nef bundles under Hall–Rado-type conditions, with applications to tautological classes and matroid Chow rings.
sections.claimed_result: The authors establish the stated Hodge–Riemann relations and extend the descent lemma to Schur classes of nef vector bundles; for products of nef (1,1)-classes, they characterize simultaneous Hodge–Riemann relations via a Hall–Rado-type condition.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Compact Kähler manifolds and nef, possibly twisted, vector bundles; principal bundle-class results assume specified Hall–Rado-type or (m,p,q)-Lefschetz conditions.
sections.unique_caveat: Conclusions are conditional, not a blanket Hodge–Riemann theorem for arbitrary nef bundles without the stated positivity assumptions.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Checked introduction connects an extension of Hodge theory to algebraic geometry and combinatorics, including applications to matroid Chow rings.

sections.title: Local Law and Eigenvector Delocalization for Random Lifts
sections.abstract: For random N-lifts of a fixed finite connected simple graph of minimum degree at least three, the authors prove a high-probability entrywise Green-function local law down to near-1/N scales away from singular energies and deduce complete eigenvector delocalization there.
sections.claimed_result: The authors obtain entrywise Green-function estimates to spectral scales (log N)^C/N in the bulk and near regular edges and cusps, then prove an eigenvector sup-norm bound of (log N)^C/sqrt(N) with high probability.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Random lifts of a fixed finite connected simple graph with minimum degree at least three; eigenvalues must stay a fixed positive distance from singular energies.
sections.unique_caveat: Singular energies are excluded, and the bounds retain logarithmic losses.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Quantitative theorem cross-listed in probability, mathematical physics, combinatorics, and spectral theory; states both a local law and a delocalization consequence.

sections.title: Escape of mass for finite-area hyperbolic surfaces
sections.abstract: The authors prove a lower bound for the L2 mass of eigenfunctions and Eisenstein series in a compact part of a noncompact finite-area hyperbolic surface, extending a result to the nonarithmetic setting.
sections.claimed_result: The authors establish the compact-region lower bound using a long-time Egorov theorem for this setting, a nonlinear uncertainty principle, and Weyl’s method for exponential sums.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Noncompact finite-area hyperbolic surfaces; eigenfunctions and Eisenstein series; the lower bound concerns their L2 norm on a compact part.
sections.unique_caveat: The abstract states a lower bound, not full equidistribution; the proof depends on the cited uncertainty principle and exponential-sum estimates.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Cross-listed across spectral theory, PDE, and dynamics; abstract identifies an extension beyond the arithmetic setting.

sections.title: Fuglede's conjecture holds in eight dimensions over the field with two elements
sections.abstract: The authors prove Fuglede’s spectral-set/tiling equivalence in F2^8, show every spectral set and tile there has a linear-subspace tiling complement, and include exact finite verification data.
sections.claimed_result: The authors prove the conjecture in dimension eight over F2 and derive a subspace-complement result; they also give a dimension-nine spectral example obstructing this Fourier-support approach at eighth density.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Nonempty subsets of finite vector spaces over F2; the equivalence is established in dimension eight with finite verification data.
sections.unique_caveat: Dimension nine remains unresolved over F2; the authors state the current Fourier-support method cannot resolve it as it stands.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Concrete conjecture resolution in a finite group, supported by ancillary programs, data, certificates, and verification logs; included in the 28 October batch despite a 26 October submission timestamp.

sections.title: Sharp well-posedness and soliton resolution for the half-wave maps equation in H1/2
sections.abstract: The authors prove optimal-threshold global well-posedness and, under a spectral assumption satisfied by a dense set of energy-space data, soliton resolution for half-wave maps on the real line, extending the results to complex Grassmannian targets.
sections.claimed_result: The authors prove global well-posedness in H1/2, ill-posedness in every Hs for s below 1/2, and asymptotic decoupling into an infinite soliton superposition under their spectral assumption.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Half-wave maps on R; soliton resolution requires the stated spectral assumption on initial data, which the authors say holds for a dense set in the energy space.
sections.unique_caveat: Soliton resolution is conditional on the spectral assumption and is not stated for every energy-space datum.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Abstract claims a sharp regularity threshold, infinite-soliton asymptotic description, and target-space extension; placement is based on concrete scope rather than attention metrics.
